title: Duties to neighbours
intro: A good neighbour is safe to live next to – and Islam teaches us to be the best neighbour on the street.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Worship Allah and do not associate anything with Him. Be good to parents, to relatives, to orphans, to the needy, to the neighbour who is near and the neighbour who is far, and to others… <small>(Qur’an, An-Nisa 4:36)</small>

The people who live near our home, on our street or in our neighbourhood are our neighbours. They are the people we meet most often and know best. Islam teaches us that besides being good to our parents and relatives, we should also be good to our neighbours.

We should respect older neighbours and greet them when we meet; with neighbours our own age we should play, hang out and be careful with each other. It is especially important to help each other in everyday tasks, which brings us even closer. A good, kind relationship with neighbours confirms our faith and gives it a special sweetness, and we feel the peace and contentment that comes from it.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “…and the best of neighbours is the one who treats his neighbour best.” (Tirmidhi)
From our parents we learned to treat our neighbours nicely: to greet them with salam when we meet, to say kind words to them, to listen to them and, if they ask for help, to help them.
The Prophet (SAW) said: “A Muslim has six rights over another Muslim: (Muslim)

items: when you meet him, give him salam;
when he asks for advice, advise him;
when he sneezes (and says Alhamdulillah), say to him yarhamukallaah;
when he is ill, visit him;
and when he dies, pray his janazah.”

learn.label: When someone sneezes and says Alhamdulillah, we say:
learn.en: May Allah have mercy on you.

learn.html: As children we get to know our first friends in our neighbourhood, and we grow up and play together. When we grow older, we go to maktab and school together and spend our free time playing.

Without good relations with neighbours there is no harmony or friendship in the jama‘ah, and no true faith. Allah (SWT) and His Messenger (SAW) strictly forbid bothering neighbours, whether they are Muslims or not, and teach us that the one who is hostile to his neighbours and neighbourhood is not a complete believer.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “By Allah, he is not a believer! By Allah, he is not a believer! By Allah, he is not a believer!” They asked: “Who, O Messenger of Allah?” He said: “The one whose neighbour is not safe from his harm.” (Bukhari)

learn.title: The woman who prayed at night
learn.html: Abu Hurairah (RA) reported that people once praised a woman to the Prophet (SAW): she prayed voluntary prayers at night, fasted besides Ramadan and gave sadaqah – but she hurt her neighbours with her tongue. The Prophet (SAW) said: “There is no good in her. She is among the people of the Fire.”
By treating children our own age kindly, we get used to good manners towards everyone. When we take care not to hurt others or call them ugly nicknames, we build a good picture of ourselves.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Always greet your neighbours nicely with a smile and salam, talk with them, and ask how they are.

practice.title: The six rights of a Muslim
practice.prompt: Put the six rights in the order the Prophet (SAW) listed them.
items: When you meet him, give him salam
When he asks for advice, advise him
When he is ill, visit him
When he dies, pray his janazah

practice.title: Good neighbour or not?
practice.prompt: Is this what a good neighbour does?

items.text: Smiling and saying salam over the fence
Shovelling snow for an older neighbour
Bringing a plate of food on Eid
Visiting a neighbour who is ill
Playing loud music late at night
Calling the neighbour’s kid an ugly nickname
Throwing rubbish into the neighbour’s yard

options: People who live near our home, on our street or in our neighbourhood

questions.q: Who is the best neighbour, according to the hadith?
options: The one who treats his neighbour best
The one with the biggest house

questions.q: Whom did the Prophet (SAW) say is “not a believer” three times?
options: The one whose neighbour is not safe from his harm
The one who lives far away
The one who has no neighbours

questions.q: Is it allowed to bother a neighbour who is not Muslim?
options: No – bothering any neighbour is forbidden

questions.q: Why was there “no good” in the woman who prayed and fasted?
options: She hurt her neighbours with her tongue

questions.q: What do we say to someone who sneezes and says Alhamdulillah?

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 Whom do we call our neighbours? What are our duties to them? What does a good relationship with neighbours mean?
🔎 Task 1: Find out how the Prophet (SAW) treated his neighbours who were not Muslims.
🤝 Task 2: Find a way to help a neighbour who needs help. Write what you did and how you helped.
